name: Mare Tranquillitatis
subtitle: Sea of Tranquility
description: A basaltic plain on the Moon's near side. Apollo 11's landing site (Tranquillity Base) sits at its south-western edge.

name: Mare Serenitatis
subtitle: Sea of Serenity
description: A round, dark basin north-east of Mare Tranquillitatis. Apollo 17 landed at its south-eastern margin in the Taurus-Littrow valley.

name: Mare Imbrium
subtitle: Sea of Showers
description: One of the largest impact basins on the Moon — about 1240 km across, formed ~3.85 billion years ago. Apollo 15 landed at its eastern edge near Hadley Rille.

name: Mare Crisium
subtitle: Sea of Crises
description: An isolated round mare on the eastern near side, easily visible to the naked eye. The Soviet Luna 24 sample-return mission landed here in 1976.

name: Oceanus Procellarum
subtitle: Ocean of Storms
description: The largest mare region on the Moon, spanning over 2500 km of the western near side. Apollo 12 landed here, near the older Surveyor 3 probe.

name: Tycho
description: A bright ray crater 86 km wide in the southern highlands, formed about 108 million years ago. Its rays radiate over much of the near side at full Moon.

name: Copernicus
description: A young (~800 million years) 93 km crater with terraced walls and a central peak, ringed by a prominent ejecta system across Mare Insularum.

name: Plato
description: A 101 km crater with an unusually dark lava-flooded floor, perched on the northern shore of Mare Imbrium. Easy to spot in any small telescope.

name: Aristarchus
description: The brightest large feature on the Moon's near side — a 40 km young crater in Oceanus Procellarum. Site of recurring transient lunar phenomena.

name: Kepler
description: A small (32 km) but bright young crater in Oceanus Procellarum, with a striking ray system that overlaps with Copernicus's to the east.

name: Apollo 11
subtitle: Tranquillity Base
description: First crewed lunar landing — Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin set foot here on 20 July 1969. Located in southern Mare Tranquillitatis.

name: Apollo 14
subtitle: Fra Mauro
description: Third crewed lunar landing, February 1971. Targeted highland material thought to be ejecta from the Imbrium impact. Alan Shepard hit golf balls here.

name: Apollo 15
subtitle: Hadley-Apennine
description: Fourth crewed landing, July 1971 — first to use the Lunar Roving Vehicle. Sampled the Apennine Mountains and the meandering Hadley Rille channel.

name: Apollo 17
subtitle: Taurus-Littrow
description: Final Apollo landing, December 1972 — geologist Harrison Schmitt's mission to a highland-mare boundary. The last crewed visit to the Moon to date.

name: Chang'e 5
subtitle: Mons Rümker
description: Chinese sample-return mission, December 2020. Brought back 1.7 kg of basalt fragments dated to ~2 Ga — the youngest lunar rocks ever sampled.

name: South Pole–Aitken Basin
description: The largest known impact basin in the Solar System, ~2500 km across and 13 km deep, mostly on the Moon's far side. A target of multiple proposed sample-return missions.
